questions.prompt: Match each element to its symbol.
questions.explain: Na, Cu, Ag and K come from Latin names: natrium, cuprum, argentum, kalium.

questions.prompt: How many atoms in total are in one molecule of methane, CH₄?
How many OXYGEN atoms are in one molecule of sulfuric acid, H₂SO₄?
questions.explain: The subscript 4 after O means four oxygen atoms.

questions.prompt: How many atoms in total are in one molecule of glucose, C₆H₁₂O₆?
What is the difference between Co and CO?
options: Co is the element cobalt; CO is a compound of carbon and oxygen
CO is an element; Co is a compound
questions.explain: A second capital letter means a new element. CO = carbon + oxygen (carbon monoxide).

questions.prompt: In the equation 'methane + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water', sort each substance.
questions.explain: Reactants are on the left of the arrow; products are on the right.

questions.prompt: Complete the word equation for burning magnesium ribbon.
questions.explain: magnesium + oxygen → magnesium oxide (the white powder left behind).

questions.prompt: Arrange the parts to make the word equation for iron reacting with sulfur.
questions.explain: iron + sulfur → iron sulfide (from the Iron + Sulfur lab in Unit 2!).

options: 2 molecules of carbon dioxide: 2 carbon and 4 oxygen atoms
questions.explain: The big number in front multiplies the whole molecule: 2 × (1 C + 2 O) = 2 C + 4 O.

questions.prompt: When you breathe out onto lime water (calcium hydroxide), it turns milky because calcium carbonate and water form. Write the word equation and name the reactants and products.
questions.modelAnswer: calcium hydroxide + carbon dioxide → calcium carbonate + water. Reactants: calcium hydroxide and carbon dioxide. Products: calcium carbonate and water.
rubric: Reactants on the left: calcium hydroxide + carbon dioxide
Products on the right: calcium carbonate + water
I used an arrow (not an equals sign) and + signs correctly
questions.explain: Word equations always go reactants → products.
